system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “key negotiated positions” are proposals, not approved Buyer positions. The Disclosure Letter supplies some useful facts, but its general disclosures and reservations do not establish that a risk has been resolved.

| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% / AUD 4.8m. | Start at 25% / AUD 6m; 20% only with Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying this draft. | **Reject for now:** no such authority has been given. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 per claim; AUD 250,000 deductible basket. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 basket, recoverable from the first dollar once exceeded. | **Counter:** the proposal raises both thresholds and converts the basket into a deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | 18 months; default application of limits to all Claims. | 24 months for general Warranty Claims only; 18 months requires Amelia’s written approval. | **Reject:** the fallback is unauthorised and must not govern other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Same cap and period as general warranties. | Separate 100% cap and at least six years, outside general thresholds and knowledge bars. | **Reject:** ownership and capacity need independent, longer protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Express carve-out for fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, thresholds, periods, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. | **Insist:** the playbook does not permit this protection to be waived. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Deemed disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records. | Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties; no blanket or prudent-search deeming. | **Delete general disclosure:** merely making material available should not qualify every warranty. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge** | Bars claims for actual or discoverable knowledge of Buyer or advisers. | Delete the blanket bar; any negotiated knowledge qualifier should identify Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, without affecting title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject:** constructive Buyer knowledge would shift undisclosed risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says final consent and evidence of conditions are absent. | Effective consent **and evidence that its conditions are satisfied** before Completion. | **Make a Completion condition:** Bluefen represents about 30% of FY26 revenue and delivery alone may not make consent effective. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; security release after Completion. | Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases at Completion. | **Reject deferred release:** a post-Completion route needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia’s approval. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 conditional bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Explicit funds-flow line item or Seller funding, including any triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs. | **Correct funds flow:** the omission must not silently transfer a Completion cost to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Narrow indemnity for SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 open, without independent proof of non-payment. | Broader protection for ownership, transfer and related loss, while preserving a verified SOW3 payment-and-confirmatory-assignment cure. | **Broaden and verify:** no receipt or assignment is supplied, but AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary and “not expected” to be material; no confirmed access, scope, notification duty or loss. | Preserve logs, investigate promptly, provide updates and address any established remediation or notification obligations. | **Require process protections:** neither a breach nor the absence of material risk is yet established. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals described as ordinary-course costs. | Assess timing, scope, accrual, avoidability and termination rights. | **Investigate, without automatic deduction:** AUD 330,000 is not yet established as Debt or a price adjustment. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limits and “settled” tax/IP terms appear intended to govern all Claims. | Distinct regimes for Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants; no hidden general-regime override. | **Revise cross-references:** a general limitation must not erase category-specific protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on the DD-012 Company share register. | Independent evidence of ownership, encumbrances, authority and ability to transfer all shares. | **Request verification:** DD-012 is a supplied internal record, not independent title proof. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Says tax and IP warranties are settled under the general regime. | Keep both open for express negotiation, without assuming unlimited liability or an agreed resolution. | **Mark unresolved:** Seller’s assertion is not Buyer approval and the operative terms need separate review. |
=== END ADVICE ===
